lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Shape and Position
lesson.summary: Flat and solid shapes, symmetry, Islamic patterns, and turns and directions.
learning_objectives: Name and describe flat and solid shapes

standards.text: Identify and describe the properties of 2-D and 3-D shapes; order and arrange mathematical objects in patterns; use mathematical vocabulary to describe position, direction and movement

success_criteria: I can name flat shapes by their sides
I can spot a line of symmetry
I can use quarter and half turns
lesson.real_life: Spotting shapes at home, patterns in mosques and giving directions.

warm_up.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?

blocks.markdown: Today we explore **shapes**, symmetry and directions.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Today we look at shapes. We meet flat shapes and solid shapes. We spot shapes that match on both sides. And we help a robot find its way.

blocks.markdown:
Flat shapes have **sides** and **corners**.

A triangle has 3 sides. A square and a rectangle have 4 sides.
blocks.say: Flat shapes are called two D shapes. Every flat shape has sides and corners. A side is a straight edge. A corner is where two sides meet. A triangle has three sides and three corners. A square has four sides and four corners. All its sides are the same length. A rectangle has four sides and four corners too. Its long sides are longer than its short sides.

scenes.say: A square. Four sides, all the same length. And four corners.

scenes.caption: Circle: 0 sides, 0 corners.
scenes.say: A circle. It has no straight sides and no corners at all. It is round all the way.

blocks.alt: A shape and its mirror image either side of a dashed fold line
blocks.caption: A line of symmetry.
blocks.say: Fold along the dashed line. Both sides match. That is a line of symmetry.

question.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?

blocks.markdown: 3 sides: triangle. 4 sides: square or rectangle. 5 sides: **pentagon**. 6 sides: **hexagon**.
blocks.say: Let us sort shapes by their sides. Shapes with three sides are triangles. Shapes with four sides are squares and rectangles. A shape with five sides is a pentagon, and with six sides a hexagon. Look around you. A door is a rectangle. A clock is a circle. A road sign can be a triangle.

blocks.title: Zara finds shapes in the mosque
blocks.transcript: Zara goes for a walk with her brother. She spots shapes everywhere. A dice is a cube. A ball is a sphere. A party hat is a cone. At the mosque there is a tile pattern. Squares and triangles repeat. Fold the star down the middle. Both halves match. That is symmetry! Zara's brother has a toy robot. It faces right. A quarter turn to the right. Now the robot faces down. Another quarter turn makes a half turn. It faces left! Shapes, symmetry and turns are everywhere. Shukriya, Zara!

blocks.markdown:
A **cube** has 6 flat faces. A **sphere** is round. A **cylinder** has 2 circles. A **cone** has a point.

Solid shapes have faces, edges and corners.
blocks.say: Solid shapes are called three D shapes. You can pick them up and hold them. A cube is like a dice. It has six flat faces, and all of them are squares. A sphere is like a ball. It is round all over. A cylinder is like a tin of beans. It has two flat circles and one curved side. A cone is like an ice cream cone. It has one flat circle and a point.

blocks.markdown:
**Symmetry** means one half is the mirror image of the other half.

The fold is the **line of symmetry**.
blocks.say: Some shapes look the same on both sides. That is called symmetry. Imagine folding a butterfly down the middle. The left wing matches the right wing exactly. The fold line is the line of symmetry, or mirror line. A butterfly, a heart and a square all have symmetry. A shape is symmetrical if one half is the mirror image of the other.

scenes.say: The right wing is the mirror image. The line down the middle is the line of symmetry.

blocks.markdown:
Islamic tile patterns use shapes that repeat, and many are symmetrical.

Look for squares, triangles and stars.
blocks.say: Many mosques have beautiful tile patterns. They use shapes that fit together with no gaps, like squares, triangles and stars. The patterns repeat again and again. Many of them are symmetrical too. Look at a pattern and ask: what shapes can I see? What repeats? Where is the mirror line?

blocks.markdown:
A **quarter turn** is a turn to the left or right. A **half turn** faces the other way.

A whole turn takes you back to the start.
blocks.say: We use turns to give directions. A quarter turn is a turn to the left or the right. A half turn takes us all the way around to face the other way. A whole turn takes us right back to where we started. Look at the robot. It faces right. If it makes a quarter turn to the right, it will face down.

blocks.markdown:
Give directions with moves and turns. Coders do this too.

Forward 2, turn right, forward 1.
blocks.say: Now be the robot's boss. Tell it to move forward two squares, then turn right, then forward one square. Where does it end up? Walk the steps yourself in the room. Giving clear directions is also what coders do when they write programs.
